catalog_quote: §3.3: Accentual languages including English are full of “phonological enclitics” that reflect prosodic reduction of syntactic words, which are then hosted in suffix-like forms by accentually stable words (isn’t, gonna, etc.). As in many languages without accents or clear prosodic indications of word boundaries, the distinction between cliticization, affixation, and simple juxtaposition is often indeterminate or at least unprovable. ... §2.1.2: There are three phonetic tone levels, but M[id] and L[ow] are essentially positional variants of a single nonhigh tone value, resulting in a phonemic two-level tone system H[igh] versus L. ... §2.1.3: Segmental and metrical phonology is relatively simple. The sequence Cvrv (where v is any short vowel) can undergo partial syncope of the first vowel. ... §3.1.1 Syllables and metrical structure: Words are normally composed of Cv and Cvv syllables.

audit.reasoning: Quote check: every quoted passage is verbatim at the stated section/page in the held Zenodo PDF of Heath & Tioté 2019. Deciding source: a 395-page 2019 reference grammar by an experienced Africanist fieldworker plus a native-region linguist, open access, Glottolog's sole grammar for mbre1244; its §2.1.2 'Tones and prosody' and ch.3 phonology describe a two-level tone system (M a positional variant of L), Cv/Cvv syllables and Cvrv syncope, and never posit word stress; the §3.3 sentence groups Pere with 'languages without accents or clear prosodic indications of word boundaries'. sources.quote: 'Three tone levels are marked in the transcription, but M-tone (e.g., ā) is a predictable development from L-tone (e.g., à).' No mention of word stress or accent; the two occurrences of 'stress(es)' (txt l.587, 591) refer to syntactic tension in SVO order, not phonological stress.

sources.note: Only other description of the language; a French-tradition 'description systématique' is likely to state explicitly whether bɛ̀rɛ́ has an accent (our no-word-stress coding rests on an oblique 'as in many languages without accents' sentence plus the absence of any stress rule in the 2019 grammar). Same authorial team and data, so it can at most make the coding explicit, not overturn it.
